<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Company&#146;s purpose shall be to perform, on its own, through third parties or in association with third parties, the study, exploration,
development and production of crude oil, natural gas and other minerals and refining, commercialization and distribution of crude oil and petroleum products and direct and indirect petroleum derivatives, including petrochemicals, chemicals,
including those derived from hydrocarbons, and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-fossil</FONT> fuels, biofuels and their components, as well as production of electric power from hydrocarbons, through which it may manufacture, use, purchase, sell,
exchange, import or export them. It shall also be the Company&#146;s purpose to render, directly, through a subsidiary or in association with third parties, telecommunications services in all forms and modalities authorized by the legislation in
force after applying for the relevant licenses as required by the regulatory framework, as well as the production, industrialization, processing, commercialization, conditioning, transportation and stockpiling of grains and products derived from
grains, as well as any other activity complementary to its industrial and commercial business or any activity which may be necessary to attain its objective. In order to fulfill these objectives, the Company may set up, become associated with or
have an interest in any public or private entity domiciled in Argentina or abroad, within the limits set forth in the Bylaws. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Filing with the

No.&nbsp;5,109, Book 113, Volume A, Sociedades An&oacute;nimas, with the above mentioned Public Registry. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Duration of the Company </U></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>2.a) Applicable accounting framework </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The condensed interim
consolidated financial statements of the Company for the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2024 are presented in accordance with IAS 34 &#147;Interim Financial Reporting&#148;. Therefore, they should be read together with the annual
consolidated financial statements of the Company as of December&nbsp;31, 2023 (&#147;annual consolidated financial statements&#148;) presented in U.S. dollars and in accordance with IFRS as issued by the IASB. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">These condensed interim consolidated financial statements corresponding to the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2024 are unaudited. The Company
believes they include all necessary adjustments to reasonably present the results of each period on a basis consistent with the audited annual consolidated financial statements. Net Income for the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2024 does
not necessarily reflect the proportion of the Group&#146;s full-year net income. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>2.b) Material accounting policies </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The material accounting policies are described in Note 2.b) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The accounting policies adopted in the preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements are consistent with those used in the
preparation of the annual consolidated financial statements, except for the valuation policy for income tax detailed in Note 18. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Functional
currency </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As mentioned in Note 2.b.1) to the annual consolidated financial statements, YPF has defined the U.S. dollar as its functional currency.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The consolidated financial statements used by YPF for statutory, legal and regulatory purposes in Argentina are those in pesos and filed with the CNV
and approved by the Board of Directors and authorized to be issued on May&nbsp;9, 2024. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:1pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:190pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Adoption of new standards and interpretations effective as from January</U><U></U><U>&nbsp;1,
2024</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Company has adopted all new and revised standards and interpretations, issued by the IASB, relevant to its operations which are of
mandatory and effective application as of March&nbsp;31, 2024, as described in Note 2.b.14) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Standards and interpretations issued by the IASB as of January</U><U></U><U>&nbsp;1, 2024 whose application is not mandatory at the closing date of
these condensed interim consolidated financial statements and have not been adopted by the Group</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In accordance with Article 1, Chapter III, Title
IV of the CNV Rules, the early application of IFRS and/or their amendments is not permitted for issuers filing financial statements with the CNV, unless specifically admitted by such agency. </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>IFRS 18 &#147;Presentation and disclosure in financial statements&#148; </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In April 2024, the IASB issued IFRS 18, which replaces IAS 1 &#147;Presentation of financial statements&#148;, with the objective of providing better
information on the financial performance of entities, improving their comparability, which is applicable to fiscal years beginning on or after January&nbsp;1, 2027. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">IFRS 18 introduces the following information requirements that can be grouped into 2 main groups: </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Group income and expenses into three defined categories: (i)&nbsp;operating; (ii) financing and (iii)&nbsp;investing,
and include certain defined subtotals, such as the operating result and the result before financing and income tax, with the aim of improving the comparability of the statement of comprehensive income. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Provide more information about the performance measures defined by management, which, although not mandatory, in the
event of including this type of measures, the entity must disclose the reason why said measures are useful to financial statements users, their method of calculation, a reconciliation between to the most directly comparable subtotal from the
statement of comprehensive income, among others. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Additionally, IFRS 18 establishes more detailed guidance on how to organize
information within the financial statements and whether it should be provided in the primary financial statements or in the notes, with the aim of improving the grouping of information in the financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the Group is in the process of evaluating the effects of the
application of IFRS 18. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>2.c) Significant estimates and key sources of estimation uncertainty </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In preparing the financial statements at a certain date, the Group is required to make estimates and assessments affecting the amount of assets and
liabilities recorded and the contingent assets and liabilities disclosed at such date, as well as income and expenses recognized in the period. Actual future profit or loss might differ from the estimates and assessments made at the date of
preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The assumptions relating to the future and other sources of uncertainty
about the estimates made for the preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements are consistent with those used by the Group in the preparation of the annual consolidated financial statements, which are disclosed in Note
2.c) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:210pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>2.d) Comparative information </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Amounts and other information corresponding to the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2023 are an integral part of these condensed interim consolidated
financial statements and are intended to be read only in relation to these financial statements. Amounts corresponding to the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2023 presented in these financial statements for comparison purposes correspond to
the functional currency of the company according to IAS&nbsp;21 (see Note 2.b)). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Additionally, from this fiscal year, the Group has made a change in
the presentation of the items in the &#147;Financial results, net&#148; line item in the statement of comprehensive income (see Note 29). This change is intended to provide more relevant and detailed information on the origin of financial results
and the effects of transactions or conditions that affect the financial situation, financial performance and cash flows of the Group such as interests and exchange differences generated by loans, among others; and improve the comparability of the
Group&#146;s financial statements with its peers. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B><A NAME="item1toc836705_10"></A>3.</B></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify"><B>SEASONALITY OF OPERATIONS </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Historically, the Group&#146;s results have been subject to seasonal fluctuations throughout the year, particularly as a result of the increase in natural
gas sales during the winter driven by the increased demand in the residential segment. Consequently, the Group is subject to seasonal fluctuations in its sales volumes and prices, with higher sales of natural gas during the winter at higher prices.
</P> <P STYLE="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B><A NAME="item1toc836705_11"></A>4.</B></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify"><B>ACQUISITIONS AND DISPOSALS </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Dissolution of the company YPF International </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On
May&nbsp;6, 2024, the Plurinational Service of Registry of Commerce (&#147;SEPREC&#148; by its acronym in Spanish) of Bolivia approved the dissolution and liquidation of YPF International. </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B><A NAME="item1toc836705_12"></A>5.</B></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify"><B>FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group&#146;s activities expose it to a variety of financial risks: Market risk (including exchange rate risk, interest rate risk, and price risk),
credit risk and liquidity risk. Within the Group, risk management functions are conducted in relation to financial risks associated to financial instruments to which the Group is exposed during a certain period or as of a specific date. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2024, there were no significant changes in the administration or policies of risk management
implemented by the Group as described in Note 4 to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:1pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="font-size:265pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="right">HORACIO DANIEL MARIN </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="right">President&#8195;&#8195;&#8195;&#8195;&#8195; </P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Liquidity risk management </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Most of the Group&#146;s loans contain market-standard covenants for contracts of this nature, which include financial covenants in respect of the
Group&#146;s leverage ratio and debt service coverage ratio, and events of defaults triggered by materially adverse judgements, among others. See Notes 16, 32 and 33 to the annual consolidated financial statements and Notes 17 and 33. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group monitors compliance with covenants on a quaterly basis. As of March&nbsp;31, 2024, the Group is in compliace with its covenants. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It should be noted that, under the terms and conditions of the loans that our subsidiary Metrogas has taken, the interest coverage ratio would not have
been complied with, which could have accelerated the maturities of these financial liabilities. However, the financial creditors formally accepted to waive Metrogas from complying with the contractual obligation related to such financial ratio, as
of March&nbsp;31, 2024. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B><A NAME="item1toc836705_13"></A>6.</B></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify"><B>BUSINESS SEGMENT INFORMATION </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The different business segments in which the Group&#146;s organization is structured consider the different activities from which the Group can obtain
revenues and incur expenses. Such organizational structure is based on the way in which the chief decision maker analyzes the main operating and financial magnitudes for making decisions about resource allocation and performance assessment, also
considering the business strategy of the Group. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Business segment information is presented consistently with the manner of reporting the information
used by the chief decision maker to allocate resources and assess business segment performance. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The business segment structure is organized as
follows: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Upstream </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Upstream business segment performs all activities related to the exploration and exploitation and production of crude oil, natural gas
and frac sand for well drilling/fracking purposes. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are largely derived from: (i)&nbsp;the sale of the crude oil produced
to the Downstream business segment; and (ii)&nbsp;the sale of the natural gas produced and the sale of the natural gas retained in plant to the Gas and Power business segment. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs related to the activities mentioned above. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Downstream </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Downstream business segment performs activities related to: (i)&nbsp;crude oil refining and the production of petrochemical products;
(ii)&nbsp;logistics related to the transportation of crude oil to the refineries and the transportation and distribution of refined and petrochemical products to be marketed at the different sales channels; (iii)&nbsp;commercialization of refined
and petrochemical products obtained from such processes; (iv)&nbsp;commercialization of crude oil; and (v)&nbsp;commercialization of specialties for the agribusiness industry and of grains and their
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">by-products.</FONT> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are derived primarily from the sale of crude oil, refined and
petrochemical products, specialties for the agribusiness industry and grains and their <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">by-products.</FONT> These operations are performed through the businesses of B2C (Retail), B2B (Industries, Transportation,
Aviation, Agro, Lubricants and Specialties), LPG, Chemicals, International Trade and Transportation and Sales to Companies. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs
all costs related to the activities mentioned above, including the purchase of crude oil from the Upstream business segment and third parties and the purchase of natural gasoline, propane and butane and natural gas to be consumed in the refinery and
petrochemical industrial complexes from the Gas and Power business segment. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Gas and Power </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Gas and Power business segment performs activities related to: (i)&nbsp;natural gas transportation to third parties and the Downstream
business segment and its commercialization; (ii)&nbsp;commercial and technical operation of the LNG regasification terminal in Escobar by hiring regasification vessels; (iii)&nbsp;transportation, conditioning and processing of natural gas retained
in plant for the separation and fractionation of natural gasoline, propane and butane; (iv)&nbsp;distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas; and (v)&nbsp;the storage of the natural gas produced. Also, through our investments in
associates and joint ventures, the Gas and Power business segment undertakes activities related to: (i)&nbsp;separation of natural gas liquids and their fractionation, storage and transportation for the production of ethane, propane, butane and
natural gasoline; (ii)&nbsp;generation of conventional thermal electric power and renewable energy; and (iii)&nbsp;production, storage, distribution and sale of fertilizers. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are largely derived from the commercialization of natural gas as producers to third parties and the Downstream business
segment, the distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas, the sale of natural gasoline, propane and butane to the Downstream business segment and the provision of LNG regasification services. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs related to the activities mentioned above, including the purchase of natural gas and natural gas retained in plant
from the Upstream business segment. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">This segment covers other activities performed by the Group not falling under the business segments mentioned above and which are not
reporting business segments, mainly comprising corporate administrative expenses and assets and construction activities. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Sales between business
segments were made at internal transfer prices established by the Group, which generally seek to approximate domestic market prices. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Operating profit
or loss and assets of each business segment have been determined after consolidation adjustments. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:190pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

period ended March&nbsp;31, 2024, there have been no changes in macroeconomic circumstances that significantly affect the Group&#146;s financial instruments measured at fair value. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2024, there were no transfers between the different hierarchies used to determine the fair value of the
Group&#146;s financial instruments. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Fair value of financial assets and financial liabilities measured at amortized cost </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The estimated fair value of loans, considering unadjusted listed prices (Level 1) for NO and interest rates offered to the Group (Level 3) for the
remaining financial loans, amounted to 8,215 and 7,547 as of March&nbsp;31, 2024 and December&nbsp;31, 2023, respectively. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The fair value of other
receivables, trade receivables, investments in financial assets, cash and cash equivalents, other liabilities and accounts payable at amortized cost, do not differ significantly from their book value. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>9. PROPERTY, PLANT AND EQUIPMENT (cont.) </B></P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group capitalizes the financial cost of loans as part of the cost of the property, plant and

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc836705_25"></A>18. INCOME TAX </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">According to IAS 34, income tax expense is recognized in each interim period based on the best estimate of the effective income tax rate expected as of
the closing date of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, considering the tax criteria that the Group assumes to apply during the fiscal year. If the estimate of such rate is modified based on new elements of judgment, the
income tax expense could require adjustments in subsequent periods. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In relation to such tax criteria, the income tax expense contemplates the
application of the integral inflation adjustment mechanism applicable to property, plant and equipment, and the indexation of the accumulated tax losses carryforward until the concurrence of the projected tax result of the fiscal year 2024, all
considering that the assumption of confiscation would be verified in accordance with the jurisprudence of the CSJN in force as of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Company considers having strong arguments to successfully defend such assumed tax criteria, in the event of a possible controversy with the tax
authorities, in accordance with the guidelines of IFRIC 23 &#147;Uncertainty over income tax treatments&#148;. As of March&nbsp;31, 2024, the assumed tax criteria generates a profit of 260. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The income tax charge for the three-month period ending March&nbsp;31, 2024 is a profit of 121. The amount accrued for the three-periods ending
March&nbsp;31, 2024 and 2023 is as follows: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc836705_38"></A>31. SHAREHOLDERS&#146; EQUITY </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of March&nbsp;31, 2024, the Company&#146;s capital amounts to 3,919 and treasury shares amount to 14 represented by 393,312,793 book-entry shares of
common stock and divided into four classes of shares (A, B, C and D), with a par value of 10 pesos and 1 vote per share. These shares are fully subscribed, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">paid-in</FONT> and authorized for stock exchange listing.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of March&nbsp;31, 2024, there are 3,764 Class&nbsp;A outstanding shares. As long as any Class&nbsp;A share remains outstanding, the affirmative
vote of the Argentine Government is required for: (i)&nbsp;mergers; (ii) acquisitions of more than 50% of YPF shares in an agreed or hostile bid; (iii)&nbsp;transfers of all the YPF&#146;s production and exploration rights; (iv)&nbsp;the voluntary
dissolution of YPF; (v)&nbsp;change of corporate and/or tax address outside Argentina; or (vi)&nbsp;make an acquisition that would result in the purchaser holding 15% or more of the Company&#146;s capital stock, or 20% or more of the outstanding
Class&nbsp;D shares. Items (iii)&nbsp;and (iv) also require prior approval by the Argentine Congress. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;26, 2024, the General
Shareholders&#146; Meeting was held, which approved the statutory financial statements of YPF (see Note 2.b)) corresponding to the year ended on December&nbsp;31, 2023 and, additionally, approved the following in relation to the retained earnings:
(i)&nbsp;completely disaffect the reserve for future dividends, the reserve for purchase of treasury shares and the reserve for investments; (ii)&nbsp;absorb accumulated losses in unappropriated retained earnings and losses up to the amount of
1,003,419&nbsp;million of pesos (US$ 1,244 million); (iii) allocate the amount of 28,745&nbsp;million of pesos (US$ 36 million) to constitute a reserve for purchase of treasury shares; and (iv)&nbsp;allocate the amount of 3,418,972&nbsp;million of
pesos (US$ 4,236 million) to constitute a reserve for investments. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the three-month periods ended March&nbsp;31, 2024 and 2023, the Company has
not repurchased any of its own shares. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc836705_39"></A>32. EARNINGS PER SHARE </B></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On March&nbsp;27, 2024, SE Resolution No.&nbsp;41/2024 was published in the BO, which approved natural gas prices at the PIST corresponding to the awarded
volumes entered into within the framework of the Plan GasAr 2023-2028 which will be applicable for natural gas consumptions made: (i)&nbsp;from April&nbsp;1 and until April&nbsp;30, 2024; (ii) from May&nbsp;1 and until September&nbsp;30, 2024; and
(iii)&nbsp;from October&nbsp;1 and until December&nbsp;31, 2024. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.e) Tax regulations </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2024, there were no significant updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.e) to the
annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.f) Custom regulations </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2024, there were no significant updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.f) to the
annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.g) Regulations related to the Foreign Exchange Market </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.g) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the three-month period ended
March&nbsp;31, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;18, 2024, the BCRA issued Communication &#147;A&#148; 7,994 which allows the possibility of
applying the collection of exports to the payment of capital and interest on financial debts abroad that are settled in the Foreign Exchange Market from April&nbsp;19, 2024 and as long as the following conditions are met: (i)&nbsp;the average life
of the debt is not less than 3 years; and (ii)&nbsp;the first capital payment is not made before the year it was entered and settled in the Foreign Exchange Market; and established the possibility of not filing for the BCRA&#146;s prior approval
process more than 3 days before the maturity of the capital and interest for access to the Foreign Exchange Market when debt payments abroad are anticipated and as long as the following conditions are met: (i)&nbsp;the access occurs simultaneously
with the settlement of a new financial debt granted by a local financial entity from a line of credit from abroad as of April&nbsp;19, 2024; (ii) the average life of the new debt is greater than the average remaining life of the anticipated debt;
and (ii)&nbsp;the accumulated amount of principal maturities of the new indebtedness does not exceed the accumulated amount of principal maturities of the anticipated debt. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.h) Decree of Necessity and Urgency (&#147;DNU&#148; by its acronym in Spanish) No.&nbsp;70/2023 </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.h) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the three-month period ended
March&nbsp;31, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On March&nbsp;14, 2024, the Chamber of Senators of the National Congress rejected the Decree
No.&nbsp;70/2023, and, as of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, is pending to be considered by the Chamber of Deputies of the National Congress. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;30, 2024, the Chamber of Deputies of the National Congress approved the proposed legislative bill called &#147;Bases and Starting Points for
the Freedom of Argentines&#148; and as of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, it is in treatment by the Chamber of Senators of the National Congress. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, it is not possible to predict the evolution of these measures or
their impacts. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:120pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.i) CNV regulatory framework </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Information requirements as Settlement and Clearing Agent and Trading Agent </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the Company is registered in the CNV under the category
&#147;Settlement and Clearing Agent and Trading Agent - Direct Participant&#148;, record No.&nbsp;549. Considering the Company&#146;s business and the CNV Rules, the Company will not, under any circumstance, offer brokerage services to third parties
for transactions in markets under the jurisdiction of the CNV, and it will also not open operating accounts to third parties to issue orders and trade in markets under the jurisdiction of the CNV. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In accordance with the CNV Rules, the Company is subject to the provisions of Article 5 c), Chapter II, Title VII of the CNV Rules, &#147;Settlement and
Clearing Agent - Direct Participant&#148;. In this respect, as set forth in Article 13, Chapter II, Title VII, of the CNV Rules, as of March&nbsp;31, 2024, the equity of the Company exceeds the minimum equity required by such Rules. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36. BALANCES AND TRANSACTIONS WITH RELATED PARTIES (cont.) </B></P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Additionally, the Group has entered into certain financing and insurance transactions with entities
related to the national public sector. Such transactions consist of certain financial transactions that are described in Notes 15, 16 and 22 and transactions with Naci&oacute;n Seguros S.A. related to certain insurance policies contracts. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On the other hand, the Group holds Bonds of the Argentine Republic 2029 and 2030 and BCRA bonds identified as investments in financial assets at fair
value through profit or loss, and bills and bonds issued by the National Government and BCRA bonds identified as investments in financial assets at amortized cost (see Note 15). Additionally, the Group holds BCRA bills identified as cash and cash
equivalents (see Note 16). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Furthermore, YPF has an indirect <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-controlling</FONT> interest in
Compa&ntilde;&iacute;a de Hidrocarburo No Convencional S.R.L. (&#147;CHNC&#148;). During the three-month periods ended March&nbsp;31, 2024 and 2023, YPF and CHNC carried out transactions, among others, the purchases of crude oil by YPF for 115 and
141, respectively. These transactions were consummated in accordance with the general and regulatory conditions of the market. The net balance payable to CHNC as of March&nbsp;31, 2024 and December&nbsp;31, 2023 amounts to 85 and 38, respectively.
See Note 36 to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of March&nbsp;31, 2024, the balance of trade receivables owed by CAMMESA to the Group
amounts to 160, including interest accrued, with 72 being overdue and pending payment. Likewise, as of March&nbsp;31, 2024, and in relation to our joint ventures YPF EE and CT Barrag&aacute;n, the balances of trade receivables owed by CAMMESA,
including interest accrued, amount to 131 and 62, respectively, being overdue and pending payment 76 and 29, respectively. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On May&nbsp;8, 2024, SE
Resolution No.&nbsp;58/2024 was published in the BO, which establishes an exceptional, transitory and unique payment regime for the balance of the MEM&#146;s economic transactions of December 2023, January 2024 and February 2024 corresponding to the
MEM&#146;s creditors, and instructs CAMMESA to determine the amounts owed to each of them corresponding to such economic transactions, which will be cancelled as follows: (i)&nbsp;the economic transactions of December 2023 and January 2024, will be
cancelled through the delivery of government securities denominated &#147;Bonos de la Rep&uacute;blica Argentina en D&oacute;lares Estadounidenses Step Up 2038&#148;; and (ii)&nbsp;the economic transactions of February 2024 will be cancelled with
the funds available in the bank accounts enabled in CAMMESA for collection purposes and with those funds available from the transfers made by the National Goverment to the &#147;Fondo Unificado con Destino al Fondo de Estabilizaci&oacute;n&#148;.

<TD VALIGN="top" COLSPAN="5"> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>NOTES TO THE CONDENSED INTERIM CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>AS OF MARCH 31, 2024 AND COMPARATIVE INFORMATION</B></P></TD></TR>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc836705_44"></A>37. EMPLOYEE BENEFIT PLANS AND SIMILAR OBLIGATIONS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Note 37 to the annual consolidated financial statements describes the main characteristics and accounting treatment for employee benefit plans and similar
obligations implemented by the Group. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In April 2024, the Company adopted the &#147;Value generation Plan&#148;, which is a long-term remuneration
program for eligible members of management of YPF with the objective of incentivizing extraordinary results in the long term and retaining key employees. Under this Plan, the Company granted 4.6&nbsp;million performance stock appreciation rights
(&#147;PSARs&#148;) to plan participants comprising key employees of the Company. The PSARs provide beneficiaries the opportunity to receive an award to be settled in cash equivalent to the appreciation in the value of the common shares of the
Company over a specified period of time. The amount to be paid upon exercise is the difference between the per share base price determined by the plan and the per share market value of the Company&#146;s common shares as of the exercise date. The
PSARs expire five years after their grant and begin to vest in the third year, subject to the fulfillment of certain conditions, including performance milestones related to the price of the Company&#146;s common shares ranging from a minimum of US
$30 per common share up to US$ 60 per common share. The beneficiaries of the PSARs are also required to remain in the Company for three years from the granting of the plan. The PSARs granted by the Company have a base price of US$ 16.17 per share,
resulting in a weighted average fair value of US$ 8.75 per PSAR as of the granting date. The Value Generation Plan was approved by the Compensation and Nomination Committee of the Company with the support of a management consulting firm (Mercer)
which advised on its design and implementation. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Note 2.b.11) to the annual consolidated financial statements describes the accounting policies for
share-based benefit plans. Repurchases of treasury shares are disclosed in Note 31. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Retirement plan</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense related to the Retirement Plan was 1 and 1 for the three-month periods ended March&nbsp;31, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Objective performance bonus programs and performance evaluation programs</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense related to the bonus programs for objectives and performance evaluation was 15 and 22 for the three-month periods ended
March&nbsp;31, 2024 and 2023, respectively. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Share-based benefit plans</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense in relation with the share-based plans was 1 and 1 to be settled in equity instruments, and 4 and 3 to be settled in cash,
for the three-month periods ended March&nbsp;31, 2024 and 2023, respectively. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:120pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:175pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="right">HORACIO DANIEL MARIN </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="right">President&#8195;&#8195;&#8195;&#8195;&#8195; </P>

in association with third parties, telecommunications services in all forms and modalities authorized by the legislation in force after applying for the relevant licenses as required by the regulatory framework, as well as the production,
industrialization, processing, commercialization, conditioning, transportation and stockpiling of grains and products derived from grains, as well as any other activity complementary to its industrial and commercial business or any activity which
may be necessary to attain its objective. In order to fulfill these objectives, the Company may set up, become associated with or have an interest in any public or private entity domiciled in Argentina or abroad, within the limits set forth in the

</A>2. BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONDENSED INTERIM CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>2.a) Applicable accounting framework </B></P>

with IAS 34 &#147;Interim Financial Reporting&#148;. Therefore, they should be read together with the annual consolidated financial statements of the Company as of December&nbsp;31, 2023 (&#147;annual consolidated financial statements&#148;)
presented in accordance with IFRS as issued by the IASB. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Moreover, some additional information required by the LGS and/or CNV&#146;s Rules have been

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Adoption of new standards and interpretations effective as from January</U><U></U><U>&nbsp;1,
2024</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Company has adopted all new and revised standards and interpretations, issued by the IASB, relevant to its operations which are of

<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Standards and interpretations issued by the IASB as of January</U><U></U><U>&nbsp;1, 2024 whose application is not mandatory at the closing date of
these condensed interim consolidated financial statements and have not been adopted by the Group</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In accordance with Article 1, Chapter III, Title
IV of the CNV Rules, the early application of IFRS and/or their amendments is not permitted for issuers filing financial statements with the CNV, unless specifically admitted by such agency. </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>IFRS 18 &#147;Presentation and disclosure in financial statements</B>&#148; </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In April 2024, the IASB issued IFRS 18, which replaces IAS 1 &#147;Presentation of financial statements&#148;, with the objective of providing better
information on the financial performance of entities, improving their comparability, which is applicable to fiscal years beginning on or after January&nbsp;1, 2027. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">IFRS 18 introduces the following information requirements that can be grouped into 2 main groups: </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="3%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Group income and expenses into three defined categories: (i)&nbsp;operating; (ii) financing and (iii)&nbsp;investing,
and include certain defined subtotals, such as the operating result and the result before financing and income tax, with the aim of improving the comparability of the statement of comprehensive income. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="3%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Provide more information about the performance measures defined by management, which, although not mandatory, in the
event of including this type of measures, the entity must disclose the reason why said measures are useful to financial statements users, their method of calculation, a reconciliation between to the most directly comparable subtotal from the
statement of comprehensive income, among others. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Additionally, IFRS 18 establishes more detailed guidance on how to organize
information within the financial statements and whether it should be provided in the primary financial statements or in the notes, with the aim of improving the grouping of information in the financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the Group is in the process of evaluating the effects of the
application of IFRS 18. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>2.c) Significant estimates and key sources of estimation uncertainty </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In preparing the financial statements at a certain date, the Group is required to make estimates and assessments affecting the amount of assets and
liabilities recorded and the contingent assets and liabilities disclosed at such date, as well as income and expenses recognized in the period. Actual future profit or loss might differ from the estimates and assessments made at the date of
preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The assumptions relating to the future and other sources of uncertainty
about the estimates made for the preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements are consistent with those used by the Group in the preparation of the annual consolidated financial statements, which are disclosed in Note
2.c) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:120pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc836705_9"></A>3. &#8201;SEASONALITY OF OPERATIONS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Historically, the Group&#146;s results have been subject to seasonal fluctuations throughout the year, particularly as a result of the increase in natural
gas sales during the winter driven by the increased demand in the residential segment. Consequently, the Group is subject to seasonal fluctuations in its sales volumes and prices, with higher sales of natural gas during the winter at higher prices.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc836705_10"></A>4. &#8201;ACQUISITIONS AND DISPOSALS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Dissolution of the company YPF International</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On
May&nbsp;6, 2024, the Plurinational Service of Registry of Commerce (&#147;SEPREC&#148; by its acronym in Spanish) of Bolivia approved the dissolution and liquidation of YPF International. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc836705_11"></A>5. &#8201;FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group&#146;s activities expose it to a variety of financial risks: Market risk (including exchange rate risk, interest rate risk, and price risk),
credit risk and liquidity risk. Within the Group, risk management functions are conducted in relation to financial risks associated to financial instruments to which the Group is exposed during a certain period or as of a specific date. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2024, there were no significant changes in the administration or policies of risk management
implemented by the Group as described in Note 4 to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:150pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD VALIGN="bottom"><B>Liquidity risk management</B></TD></TR>
</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Most of the Group&#146;s loans contain market-standard covenants for contracts of this nature, which include financial
covenants in respect of the Group&#146;s leverage ratio and debt service coverage ratio, and events of defaults triggered by materially adverse judgements, among others. See Notes 16, 32 and 33 to the annual consolidated financial statements and
Notes 17 and 33. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group monitors compliance with covenants on a quaterly basis. As of March&nbsp;31, 2024, the Group is in compliace with its
covenants. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It should be noted that, under the terms and conditions of the loans that our subsidiary Metrogas has taken, the interest coverage ratio
would not have been complied with, which could have accelerated the maturities of these financial liabilities. However, the financial creditors formally accepted to waive Metrogas from complying with the contractual obligation related to such
financial ratio, as of March&nbsp;31, 2024. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc836705_12"></A>6. &#8201;BUSINESS SEGMENT INFORMATION </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The different business segments in which the Group&#146;s organization is structured consider the different activities from which the Group can obtain
revenues and incur expenses. Such organizational structure is based on the way in which the chief decision maker analyzes the main operating and financial magnitudes for making decisions about resource allocation and performance assessment, also
considering the business strategy of the Group. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Business segment information is presented in U.S. dollars, the functional currency of the Company
(see Note 2.b)), consistently with the manner of reporting the information used by the chief decision maker to allocate resources and assess business segment performance. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The business segment structure is organized as follows: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Upstream </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Upstream business segment performs all activities related to the exploration and exploitation and production of crude oil, natural
gas and frac sand for well drilling/fracking purposes. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are largely derived from: (i)&nbsp;the sale of the crude oil
produced to the Downstream business segment; and (ii)&nbsp;the sale of the natural gas produced and the sale of the natural gas retained in plant to the Gas and Power business segment. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs related to the activities mentioned above. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Downstream business segment performs activities related to: (i)&nbsp;crude oil refining and the production of petrochemical products;
(ii)&nbsp;logistics related to the transportation of crude oil to the refineries and the transportation and distribution of refined and petrochemical products to be marketed at the different sales channels; (iii)&nbsp;commercialization of refined

petrochemical industrial complexes from the Gas and Power business segment. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Gas and Power business segment performs activities related to: (i)&nbsp;natural gas transportation to third parties and the
Downstream business segment and its commercialization; (ii)&nbsp;commercial and technical operation of the LNG regasification terminal in Escobar by hiring regasification vessels; (iii)&nbsp;transportation, conditioning and processing of natural gas
retained in plant for the separation and fractionation of natural gasoline, propane and butane; (iv)&nbsp;distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas; and (v)&nbsp;the storage of the natural gas produced. Also, through our
investments in associates and joint ventures, the Gas and Power business segment undertakes activities related to: (i)&nbsp;separation of natural gas liquids and their fractionation, storage and transportation for the production of ethane, propane,
butane and natural gasoline; (ii)&nbsp;generation of conventional thermal electric power and renewable energy; and (iii)&nbsp;production, storage, distribution and sale of fertilizers. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are largely derived from the commercialization of natural gas as producers to third parties and the Downstream business
segment, the distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas, the sale of natural gasoline, propane and butane to the Downstream business segment and the provision of LNG regasification services. </P>

from the Upstream business segment. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc836705_24"></A>18. INCOME TAX </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">According to IAS 34, income tax expense is recognized in each interim period based on the best estimate of the effective income tax rate expected as of
the closing date of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, considering the tax criteria that the Group assumes to apply during the fiscal year. If the estimate of such rate is modified based on new elements of judgment, the
income tax expense could require adjustments in subsequent periods. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In relation to such tax criteria, the income tax expense contemplates the
application of the integral inflation adjustment mechanism applicable to property, plant and equipment, and the indexation of the accumulated tax losses carryforward until the concurrence of the projected tax result of the fiscal year 2024, all
considering that the assumption of confiscation would be verified in accordance with the jurisprudence of the CSJN in force as of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Company considers having strong arguments to successfully defend such assumed tax criteria, in the event of a possible controversy with the tax
authorities, in accordance with the guidelines of IFRIC 23 &#147;Uncertainty over income tax treatments&#148;. As of March&nbsp;31, 2024, the assumed tax criteria generates a profit of 222,717. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The income tax charge for the three-month period ending March&nbsp;31, 2024 is a profit of 103,743. The amount accrued for the three-periods ending
March&nbsp;31, 2024 and 2023 is as follows: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE CELLSPACING="0" CELLPADDING="0" WIDTH="100%" BORDER="0" STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:7pt" ALIGN="center">

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc836705_37"></A>31. SHAREHOLDERS&#146; EQUITY </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of March&nbsp;31, 2024, the Company&#146;s capital amounts to 3,919 and treasury shares amount to 14 represented by 393,312,793 book-entry shares of
common stock and divided into four classes of shares (A, B, C and D), with a par value of 10 pesos and 1 vote per share. These shares are fully subscribed, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">paid-in</FONT> and authorized for stock exchange listing.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of March&nbsp;31, 2024, there are 3,764 Class&nbsp;A outstanding shares. As long as any Class&nbsp;A share remains outstanding, the affirmative
vote of the Argentine Government is required for: (i)&nbsp;mergers; (ii) acquisitions of more than 50% of YPF shares in an agreed or hostile bid; (iii)&nbsp;transfers of all the YPF&#146;s production and exploration rights; (iv)&nbsp;the voluntary
dissolution of YPF; (v)&nbsp;change of corporate and/or tax address outside Argentina; or (vi)&nbsp;make an acquisition that would result in the purchaser holding 15% or more of the Company&#146;s capital stock, or 20% or more of the outstanding
Class&nbsp;D shares. Items (iii)&nbsp;and (iv) also require prior approval by the Argentine Congress. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;26, 2024, the General
Shareholders&#146; Meeting was held, which approved the statutory financial statements of YPF (see Note 2.b)) corresponding to the year ended on December&nbsp;31, 2023 and, additionally, approved the following in relation to the retained earnings:
(i)&nbsp;completely disaffect the reserve for future dividends, the reserve for purchase of treasury shares and the reserve for investments; (ii)&nbsp;absorb accumulated losses in unappropriated retained earnings and losses up to the amount of
1,003,419; (iii) allocate the amount of 28,745 to constitute a reserve for purchase of treasury shares; and (iv)&nbsp;allocate the amount of 3,418,972 to constitute a reserve for investments. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the three-month periods ended March&nbsp;31, 2024 and 2023, the Company has not repurchased any of its own shares. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.d) Incentive programs for hydrocarbon production </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.d) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the three-month period ended
March&nbsp;31, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Plan for Reinsurance and Promotion of Federal Hydrocarbon Production Domestic Self-Sufficiency, Exports,
Imports Substitution and the Expansion of the Transportation System for all Hydrocarbon Basins in the Country 2023-2028 (</U><U>&#147;</U><U>Plan GasAr 2023-2028</U><U>&#148;</U><U>)</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On March&nbsp;27, 2024, SE Resolution No.&nbsp;41/2024 was published in the BO, which approved natural gas prices at the PIST corresponding to the awarded
volumes entered into within the framework of the Plan GasAr 2023-2028 which will be applicable for natural gas consumptions made: (i)&nbsp;from April&nbsp;1 and until April&nbsp;30, 2024; (ii) from May&nbsp;1 and until September&nbsp;30, 2024; and
(iii)&nbsp;from October&nbsp;1 and until December&nbsp;31, 2024. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.e) Tax regulations </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2024, there were no significant updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.e) to the
annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.f) Custom regulations </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2024, there were no significant updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.f) to the
annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.g) Regulations related to the Foreign Exchange Market </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.g) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the three-month period ended
March&nbsp;31, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;18, 2024, the BCRA issued Communication &#147;A&#148; 7,994 which allows the possibility of
applying the collection of exports to the payment of capital and interest on financial debts abroad that are settled in the Foreign Exchange Market from April&nbsp;19, 2024 and as long as the following conditions are met: (i)&nbsp;the average life
of the debt is not less than 3 years; and (ii)&nbsp;the first capital payment is not made before the year it was entered and settled in the Foreign Exchange Market; and established the possibility of not filing for the BCRA&#146;s prior approval
process more than 3 days before the maturity of the capital and interest for access to the Foreign Exchange Market when debt payments abroad are anticipated and as long as the following conditions are met: (i)&nbsp;the access occurs simultaneously
with the settlement of a new financial debt granted by a local financial entity from a line of credit from abroad as of April&nbsp;19, 2024; (ii) the average life of the new debt is greater than the average remaining life of the anticipated debt;
and (ii)&nbsp;the accumulated amount of principal maturities of the new indebtedness does not exceed the accumulated amount of principal maturities of the anticipated debt. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.h) Decree of Necessity and Urgency (&#147;DNU&#148; by its acronym in Spanish) No.&nbsp;70/2023 </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.h) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the three-month period ended
March&nbsp;31, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On March&nbsp;14, 2024, the Chamber of Senators of the National Congress rejected the Decree
No.&nbsp;70/2023, and, as of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, is pending to be considered by the Chamber of Deputies of the National Congress. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;30, 2024, the Chamber of Deputies of the National Congress approved the proposed legislative bill called &#147;Bases and Starting Points for
the Freedom of Argentines&#148; and as of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, it is in treatment by the Chamber of Senators of the National Congress. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, it is not possible to predict the evolution of these measures or
their impacts. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:90pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:10pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc836705_43"></A>37. EMPLOYEE BENEFIT PLANS AND SIMILAR OBLIGATIONS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Note 37 to the annual consolidated financial statements describes the main characteristics and accounting treatment for employee benefit plans and similar
obligations implemented by the Group. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In April 2024, the Company adopted the &#147;Value generation Plan&#148;, which is a long-term remuneration
program for eligible members of management of YPF with the objective of incentivizing extraordinary results in the long term and retaining key employees. Under this Plan, the Company granted 4.6&nbsp;million performance stock appreciation rights
(&#147;PSARs&#148;) to plan participants comprising key employees of the Company. The PSARs provide beneficiaries the opportunity to receive an award to be settled in cash equivalent to the appreciation in the value of the common shares of the
Company over a specified period of time. The amount to be paid upon exercise is the difference between the per share base price determined by the plan and the per share market value of the Company&#146;s common shares as of the exercise date. The
PSARs expire five years after their grant and begin to vest in the third year, subject to the fulfillment of certain conditions, including performance milestones related to the price of the Company&#146;s common shares ranging from a minimum of US$
30 per common share up to US$ 60 per common share. The beneficiaries of the PSARs are also required to remain in the Company for three years from the granting of the plan. The PSARs granted by the Company have a base price of US$ 16.17 per share,
resulting in a weighted average fair value of US$ 8.75 per PSAR as of the granting date. The Value Generation Plan was approved by the Compensation and Nomination Committee of the Company with the support of a management consulting firm (Mercer)
which advised on its design and implementation. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Note 2.b.11) to the annual consolidated financial statements describes the accounting policies for
share-based benefit plans. Repurchases of treasury shares are disclosed in Note 31. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Retirement plan</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense related to the Retirement Plan was 753 and 239 for the three-month periods ended March&nbsp;31, 2024 and 2023,
respectively.&#8195; </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Objective performance bonus programs and performance evaluation programs</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense related to the bonus programs for objectives and performance evaluation was 12,826 and 4,577 for the three-month periods
ended March&nbsp;31, 2024 and 2023, respectively.&#8195; </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Share-based benefit plans</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense in relation with the share-based plans was 754 and 109 to be settled in equity instruments, and 2,872 and 623 to be settled
in cash, for the three-month periods ended March&nbsp;31, 2024 and 2023, respectively. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:200pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
